verses.text: Of the children of Ammon. Yahweh says: “Has Israel no sons? has he no heir? Why then does Malcam possess Gad, and his people dwell in its cities?

Therefore behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard against Rabbah of the children of Ammon; and it shall become a desolate heap, and her daughters will be burned with fire: then Israel will possess those who possessed him,” says Yahweh.

“Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste! Cry, you daughters of Rabbah! Clothe yourself in sackcloth. Lament, and run back and forth among the fences; for Malcam will go into captivity, his priests and his princes together.
Why do you boast in the valleys, your flowing valley, backsliding daughter? You trusted in her treasures, saying, ‘Who will come to me?’

Behold, I will bring a terror on you,” says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, “from all who are around you. All of you will be driven completely out, and there will be no one to gather together the fugitives.
“But afterward I will bring back the captivity of the children of Ammon,” says Yahweh.
Of Edom. Yahweh of Armies says: “Is wisdom no more in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom vanished?
Flee! Turn back! Dwell in the depths, inhabitants of Dedan; for I will bring the calamity of Esau on him when I visit him.
If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? If thieves came by night, wouldn’t they steal until they had enough?
But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he will not be able to hide himself. His offspring  is destroyed, with his brothers and his neighbors; and he is no more.
Leave your fatherless children. I will preserve them alive. Let your widows trust in me.”

For Yahweh says: “Behold, they to whom it didn’t pertain to drink of the cup shall certainly drink; and are you he who shall altogether go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, but you shall surely drink.
For I have sworn by myself,” says Yahweh, “that Bozrah will become an astonishment, a reproach, a waste, and a curse. All its cities will be perpetual wastes.”
I have heard news from Yahweh, and an ambassador is sent among the nations, saying, “Gather yourselves together! Come against her! Rise up to the battle!”
“For, behold, I have made you small among the nations, and despised among men.

As for your terror, the pride of your heart has deceived you, O you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill, though you should make your nest as high as the eagle, I will bring you down from there,” says Yahweh.
“Edom will become an astonishment. Everyone who passes by it will be astonished, and will hiss at all its plagues.
As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighbor cities,” says Yahweh, “no man will dwell there, neither will any son of man live therein.

“Behold, he will come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong habitation: for I will suddenly make them run away from it; and whoever is chosen, I will appoint him over it. For who is like me? Who will appoint me a time? Who is the shepherd who will stand before me?”

Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh, that he has taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely they will drag them away, the little ones of the flock. Surely he will make their habitation desolate over them.
The earth trembles at the noise of their fall; there is a cry, the noise which is heard in the Red Sea.
Behold, he will come up and fly as the eagle, and spread out his wings against Bozrah. The heart of the mighty men of Edom at that day will be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
Of Damascus: “Hamath is confounded, and Arpad; for they have heard evil news, they are melted away: there is sorrow on the sea; it can’t be quiet.
Damascus has grown feeble, she turns herself to flee, and trembling has seized on her: anguish and sorrows have taken hold of her, as of a woman in travail.
How is the city of praise not forsaken, the city of my joy?
Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets, and all the men of war shall be brought to silence in that day,” says Yahweh of Armies.
“I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall devour the palaces of Ben Hadad.”
Of Kedar, and of the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Yahweh says: “Arise, go up to Kedar, and destroy the children of the east.
They will take their tents and their flocks. they will carry away for themselves their curtains, all their vessels, and their camels; and they will cry to them, Terror on every side!
Flee! Wander far off! Dwell in the depths, you inhabitants of Hazor,” says Yahweh; “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has taken counsel against you, and has conceived a purpose against you.
Arise! Go up to a nation that is at ease, that dwells without care,” says Yahweh; “that has neither gates nor bars, that dwells alone.

Their camels will be a booty, and the multitude of their livestock a plunder. I will scatter to all winds those who have the corners of their beards cut off; and I will bring their calamity from every side of them,” says Yahweh.
Hazor will be a dwelling place of jackals, a desolation forever. No man shall dwell there, neither shall any son of man live therein.”
Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying,
“Yahweh of Armies says: ‘Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.
On Elam will I bring the four winds from the four quarters of the sky, and will scatter them toward all those winds. There will be no nation where the outcasts of Elam will not come.

I will cause Elam to be dismayed before their enemies, and before those who seek their life; and I will bring evil on them, even my fierce anger,’ says Yahweh; ‘and I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them;
and I will set my throne in Elam, and will destroy from there king and princes,’ says Yahweh.
‘But it shall happen in the latter days, that I will bring back the captivity of Elam,’ says Yahweh.”

footnotes.content: Yahweh sees the injustice plainly: Ammon has stolen Gad—a tribe's homeland taken by a foreign people. The Lord notices what we notice. He asks a question that carries weight: *Why* does a nation without inheritance sit where a son of Israel should dwell? Sometimes the Lord's question *is* His answer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This is the reversal a betrayed people needs to hear. Those who stole will lose their cities to ruin; those displaced will possess their land again. Yahweh's promise carries weight because He sees injustice complete, and He does not ignore the wronged.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heshbon and Rabbah were real cities; the imagery is stark—sackcloth, wailing, people running in panic through the ruins of what they thought was secure. When God withdraws His hand, earthly strength means nothing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A daughter who boasts of her valleys and her wealth—trusting in what flows and what she possesses rather than in the God who alone can keep her. Pride whispers *Who will reach me?* and we forget: the Lord reaches farthest of all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Terror on every side; no one gathers the scattered ones. This is what exile feels like to those who live it. Yet we hear it now as a warning so we might turn back to the God who, even then, could gather us if we would let Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even within judgment, the Lord keeps a door open: *Afterward*, He will bring back the captivity of Ammon. This is the shape of His mercy—the ax falls, but not the last word. Exile need not be permanent for any nation that turns.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Edom was known for wisdom—Teman was a seat of the wise. But wisdom that turns from Yahweh becomes foolishness. The prudent who refuse to hear God's counsel become the ruins of their own counsel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dedan was a trading hub in the desert; the Edomites lived in the rocky highlands. *Dwell in the depths* means hide where you can, but know: when the Lord brings calamity, there is no hiding place that holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A grape gatherer leaves some grapes; a thief steals enough and moves on. But what comes on Edom will be thorough—no mercy, no gleaning, no restraint. This is what happens when a nation's cup of rebellion fills full.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bare, uncovered, stripped of hiding places. Esau (Edom's father) was a brother to Jacob, yet here Yahweh removes every shelter—offspring, brothers, neighbors all consumed. The judgment on Edom will be total and visible to all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the midst of calamity, the Lord speaks tenderness to the vulnerable: widows and orphans. Even when judgment falls on a people, God's heart runs toward the helpless. He is the Father of the fatherless, the Guardian of the widow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some nations, the Lord says, must drink the cup of judgment even though it wasn't their burden to bear by rights. And if they must drink, how much more those who filled that cup themselves? The logic is inexorable—no one escapes accountability.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bozrah was Edom's capital. The Lord swears by Himself—the strongest oath, the deepest commitment. What He declares will stand: astonishment, waste, and a curse that echoes through generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An ambassador carries news among nations: *Come against her. Rise up to battle.* The Lord uses even hostile nations as instruments of His justice. What seems like human choice is ordered by a hand greater than any throne.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Small among the nations, despised among men. Pride falls to nothing before the Lord. Edom thought itself mighty; Yahweh reduces it to smallness so that all may see: there is no safety in earthly strength alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Edom's cities clung to rock clefts in the highlands, built so high that enemies would struggle to reach them. The height of the eagle—but Yahweh brings down even what dwells highest. No fortress survives His call.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Passersby will hiss at Edom's ruin—not in mockery, but in the sharp intake of breath we make when we see something unspeakably wrong. The remnant of a proud people becomes a sign to all: this is what distances from God brings.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Like Sodom and Gomorrah—cities that became bywords for total destruction, places so ruined that no one dwelt there. The Lord measures Edom by the same measure as those cities. The comparison carries ancient weight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A lion rises from the pride of the Jordan—swift, unstoppable, sudden. The image is wild and fierce. Then the Lord pivots: *Who is like me? Who will appoint me a time?* The Creator stands before all creatures, answerable to none.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The counsel of Yahweh against Edom is set; His purposes are fixed. The little ones of the flock—Edom's people—will be dragged away, and their habitation made desolate. What Yahweh counsels comes to pass.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The earth trembles at the fall. A cry is heard all the way to the Red Sea—the noise of collapse carries far. When a nation falls to the hand of God, the world shakes and takes notice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The eagle comes up, spreads wings against Bozrah. The mighty men of Edom—warriors, soldiers—have hearts like women in labor: helpless, terrified, unable to act. Earthly strength breaks before the Lord's decree.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Damascus, Hamath, Arpad—three Syrian cities. The message of judgment travels fast among them, and their melting away is like water losing form. Even the sea cannot keep quiet under such news.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Damascus grows feeble, turns to flee, is seized by trembling. The image is of a woman in travail—helpless, gripped by forces beyond her power. This is the condition of a city when the Lord lets judgment fall.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The city of praise, the city of joy—Damascus was known for beauty and delight. Yet the Lord speaks: How has it been abandoned? When God withdraws favor, all that made a city bright dims to nothing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Young men fall in the streets; soldiers are brought to silence. The war that comes is final—no strength remains to resist, no voice left to cry out. This is what judgment looks like when it is complete.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ben Hadad was a name carried by Syrian kings. Fire in the wall—palace fire—means the seat of power itself burns. When the throne falls, so falls all who trusted in it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kedar and Hazor were nomadic Arab kingdoms on the desert's edge. Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian king carried out what Yahweh decreed. History moves at God's direction, though human kings think they move at their own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tents, flocks, camels, vessels—the nomad's whole world is carried on animals and in the hand. When raiders come, they seize it all. *Terror on every side!* becomes their cry—no safety, no place to run.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh speaks directly to the inhabitants: Flee, wander, dwell in depths. Nebuchadnezzar's counsel against them is set; he has conceived a purpose. When empires turn their eye on a people, that people knows its time has come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A nation at ease, without care—they thought themselves safe, unguarded, dwelling alone far from empires. Yet the Lord speaks to them too. No place exists so remote that it escapes His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Camels become booty; livestock becomes plunder. The scattered ones are driven to all winds—the diaspora of a people broken. Yet even here, the Lord says *I will scatter*—His hand is at work in what seems like chaos.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hazor becomes a dwelling place of jackals—wild dogs, the sound of desolation itself. A forever emptiness. When a city falls to the Lord's judgment, it reverts to nature; humans no longer dwell there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word came to Jeremiah in the beginning of Zedekiah's reign—a fresh word from Yahweh, timed to a specific moment in history. The Lord speaks when and how He will, and His prophets carry His word faithfully.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bow of Elam was their might; their archers were known. Yahweh says He will break it—the very emblem of their strength shattered. When the Lord targets our confidence, what did we truly rest on?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four winds from the four quarters—a scattering total and complete. Elamites will be found in exile everywhere; no nation exists where they will not arrive as the scattered ones. Diaspora is the outcome Yahweh speaks.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sword follows them; the Lord's fierce anger pursues. Those who sought their life find no escape. This is judgment that does not relent—it continues, it pursues, until the account is settled.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh will set His throne in Elam. Kings and princes will be destroyed; the land will know the Lord's rule directly—not through human governance, but through the seat of divine judgment itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yet here again: *In the latter days, I will bring back the captivity of Elam.* Readers today hear an echo in these words—how many peoples and nations have discovered that the Lord's judgment, however severe, need not be the final word. Hope remains for those who, in exile or ruin, turn back to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
